title: Green beans, frozen, cooked, fat added, NS

content.title: About
content.content: Green beans (Phaseolus vulgaris) are young pods harvested before the seeds fully mature. This product is blanched, frozen, and has a plant-based fat added, with the fat type listed as NS (not specified). It offers a quick‑cook convenience while retaining most of the vegetable’s nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Green beans are a good source of B‑vitamins, vitamin C, and potassium.
Freezing immediately after cooking preserves their bright color and crisp texture.
Added fat enhances absorption of fat‑soluble nutrients such as vitamin K.
Green beans are common in Asian and Mediterranean cuisines as side dishes and salads.
Several cultivars exist, differing in pod size and shape.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber supports healthy digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and magnesium help maintain normal blood pressure, and the added plant fat may provide beneficial monounsaturated fats.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: When consumed in moderation, it fits well into calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of plant protein
items.content: Protein contributes to muscle maintenance, especially when combined with other protein sources.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to beans.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared versions may contain added salt; people monitoring sodium should check the label.

items.title: Unspecified fat type
items.content: Since the fat type is listed as NS, those with sensitivities should verify the ingredient list.

items.title: Food safety after thawing
items.content: If thawed and left at room temperature too long, bacterial growth can occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Thaw the beans in the microwave or gently on the stovetop, then heat until hot. They can be added to soups, stews, salads, pasta dishes, or served as a side seasoned with herbs, soy sauce, or lemon juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the frozen product at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 1–2 days and store in the refrigerator at 0–4 °C. Do not refreeze.
